newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Public to have input on planned SAfrica iron plant.
newsitem.headline: Public to have input on planned SAfrica iron plant.

text.p: South Africa's Industrial Development Corporation (IDC) said on Wednesday it would hold public meetings to open its proposed 5.2 billion rand iron ore reduction plant to public scrutiny.

The possibility of the waste product, magnetite, being piped to Mozambique through the Kruger National Park -- South Africa's largest game reserve -- has caused an outcry among conservationists, who fear that this could spark the widespread commercial exploitation of the reserve.
But the IDC said on Wednesday it would hold public meetings in South Africa and Mozambique to enable concerned parties to list their objections and concerns.
Magnetite is waste produced from copper operations at Phalaborwa and has been accumulating in stockpiles for more than 30 years.

The IDR (iron direct reduction) plant would provide an ideal anchor client for Mozambique's Pande gas field near Inhassorro, about 600 km northeast of Maputo, which the Mozambican government and American energy firm Enron Corp plan to develop.
Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said earlier this month that the IDR plant could be situated in Phalaborwa, Maputo or elsewhere in Mozambique.
Gas could be piped from Pande to Maputo, Phalaborwa or another site in Mozambique.
Initial estimates were that a pipeline between Phalaborwa and Maputo would cost about 900 million rand ($201 million).
Erwin said the project could earn both countries about 2.05 billion rand combined and create about 500 direct permanent jobs and another 1,600 indirect jobs.
The life expectancy of the project was estimated to be at least 30 years.
